sentences.text: This miscellaneous appeal has been preferred by Insurance Company under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is arising out of the award dated 06.07.2012 passed by First Additional Member to the Court of First Additional, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT), Guna (MP) in Claim Case No.71/2011 on account of not exonerating from liability.

entities.text: Court of First Additional, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT), Guna
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The brief facts of the case is that deceased died in a road traffic accident dated 11.08.2007 on account of rash and negligent driving of bus Bearing No.MP08-P-134.
On the fateful day, the aforesaid bus was insured with appellant- Insurance Company.

As per the respondent Nos.1 to 5,
who is LRs of the deceased filed a claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act for releasing an amount of Rs.16 lacs with regard to death of deceased Kalabai.

3. The aforesaid claim petition was opposed by the Insurance Company inter alia on the grounds that on the fateful day, the insured bus was being plied without valid permit to drive the same hence,
on account there being breach of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:17233 2 MA-971-2012 policy conditions, the company was not liable to pay any amount as compensation.

4. Learned Claims Tribunal framed the issues and recorded the evidence adduced by the respective New India Assurance Company Ltd. vs Devbux on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40410636/
1 parties.

sentences.text: Vide award impugned herein the claim application filed by the respondents No.1 to 5 has been allowed and they have been held entitled for amount of compensation of Rs.2,85,000/- along with interest @ 7% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till its realisation.

5. Being aggrieved by the impugned award, this appeal has been filed by the Insurance Company and submitted that impugned award is against the law and material available on record as well as against the settled principles of law, therefore, is liable to be set aside.

It is further submitted that at the time of accident, insured vehicle was being plied without valid permit hence, the breach of policy conditions was proved and, therefore, Insurance Company deserved exoneration from the liability as to pay any amount as compensation.
6.

It is further submitted that in his defence, Insurance Company examined Rai Singh Rajput from RTO Guna, who in his statement before the Claims Tribunal stated that permanent permit was issued by the RTO Gwalior on behalf of Insurance Company repeated efforts were made to procure presence of RTO Gwalior as witness for adducing evidence, but presence of this witness could not be procured and the learned Claims Tribunal closed the Insurance Company's right to adduce evidence.
Hence, Insurance Company deserved exoneration of the liability as to pay the amount of compensation.
7. On the other hand, counsel for the respondents has supported the award impugned and prays for rejection of this appeal.
8. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:17233 3 MA-971-2012 9.
It is well settled principle of law that it is a duty of Insurance Company to prove that Owner and Driver breach the terms and conditions of the Insurance Policy.
It must be proved by way of evidence or any other way.

10. In the present case, on perusal of the entire record, it is crystal clear that Insurance Company procured the witness from RTO Guna, namely, Rai Singh Rajput, who in his evidence deposed that permanent permit was issued from RTO Gwalior.
So it is a duty of Insurance company to call RTO Gwalior to prove that at the time of alleged incident, offending bus has no valid permit.
But perusal of order sheets of the Claims Tribunal, it was found that Insurance Company has not taken any keen interest to call RTO, Gwalior for proving his defence.
Therefore, Insurance Company is unable to prove that at the time of the alleged accident, offending vehicle has no valid permit.
11. So in the considered opinion of this Court, The Claims Tribunal has not committed any error in holding liable Insurance Company for pay amount of compensation to claimant.
12. Therefore, the impugned award passed by the Claims Tribunal is therefore affirmed.
No illegality is found in the impugned Award.
